transcript:
HEADER: Date: 2025-10-15 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 1:07:00
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Matt Chen (Redwood Platform Eng), Luis Alvarez (Redwood Support) -- Sofia Patel (Acme Head of MLOps), Ravi Kapoor (Infra), Emma Li (Security), Tom O'Neill (SRE)

AUTO-SUMMARY: SE walked through artifact delivery process for air-gapped sites; discussed NVIDIA driver packaging, offline license keys, and container runtime ops. Discussed performance tuning knobs: batching, KV cache warmup, quantization tradeoffs. Agreed next steps and bench schedule.

00:00:00 Jordan: ok everybody hi thanks for joining on time, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off and then Priya will go through the artifact and install flow.
00:14:12 Priya: hey all yeah so high level for airgapped installs we provide an "artifact bundle" which is basically tar gz of the runtime image, nvidia driver packages, kernel module and a signed offline license blob. we'll also include a small offline activation tool that runs locally, it does HSM-less activation by exchanging a signed nonce — um it's file based so nothing needs to phone home.
00:14:45 Sofia: sorry could you repeat the driver version you recommend? we've got KPIs around 1.5k token/s for our chonk prompt, we want the best perf.
00:15:02 Priya: sure — our validated combo for Ampere nodes is NVIDIA driver 535.86 with CUDA 12.2 and cuDNN 9.x, but we also support 525 series for older kernels. we'll include both in the bundle and a note on recommended kernel parameters. the 535 line gave about 8-12% better int8 throughput in our lab for Llama-2 style models when paired with our quantization profile.
00:15:31 Ravi: are you shipping the drivers as .run or as distro packages? we run RHEL 8.8 and don't want to rebuild.
00:15:44 Priya: good question — we ship both: .rpm for RHEL/CentOS and the NVIDIA .run installer as fallback. the rpm is pre-built against the kernel-rt headers we tested. we also include DKMS steps for custom kernels.
00:24:10 Matt: quick note on the runtime side — when you boot the runtime in airgap mode we pre-load the KV cache for common prefixes if you provide sample prompt sets. that helps amortize the warmup latency but it does increase memory pressure. so there's a knob in the service config to set max_prefetch_keys and max_cache_bytes.
00:24:44 Sofia: so typical cold start penalty, how long does it take to warm the KV cache for a 2B-context workload?
00:25:01 Matt: depends on your prompt mix, but if you precompute top-500 prefixes it can be under 20 seconds to reach steady throughput for the common path. without prefetching cold starts can be multiple seconds per heavy prompt though steady-state tok/s is unaffected.
00:33:05 Emma: security question — the offline license blob, is it protected? if someone copies it, can they spin up an instance?
00:33:27 Priya: the license is bound to a hardware fingerprint: mac address, a single NVMe serial, and a TPM endorsement key if present. the activation tool emits an audit file you can keep; we also sign the blob with our key and include an expiry + feature flags in the payload.
00:33:58 Emma: ok and can we rotate the key or revoke a license if a machine is decommissioned?
00:34:12 Priya: yes — we expose a revocation list and we publish CRLs as part of the quarterly artifacts. in fully air-gapped sites you do need to import the CRL file from the bundle; we support automatic scheduled pulls if you provide an internal mirror.
00:41:20 Ravi: about GPU drivers and firmware — what's the process if we need a specialized driver from Nvidia? like a vendor-specific patch?
00:41:39 Priya: we can accept vetted vendor drivers but we run an internal compatibility check. the recommended pattern is you provide the .rpm and we run a smoke bench in our lab, then add it to a custom artifact for your account. note that unsupported drivers may lose some kernel-level optimizations; we'll flag that in the runbook.
00:49:02 Sofia: let's talk perf knobs — batching and quantization. our team is sensitive to latency tail P95 — can you run with small batch sizes?
00:49:20 Matt: yes, the runtime supports dynamic batching with strict latency SLO modes. you can set max_batch_size and idle_flush_ms on a per-route basis — small batches (1-4) keep P95 low but reduce throughput. quantization helps reduce memory and boost throughput; our int8 profile reduces memory by ~45% and improves throughput by 1.6x for some models, but you should expect a small quality delta on specific prompts. we recommend running A/B prompts in your eval harness.
00:49:56 Tom: are there any gotchas with KV cache and quantized models?
00:50:12 Matt: quantization changes token scoring slightly so cache hit semantics are the same, but you might see different beam ordering in some cases. KV cache is storage of hidden states — it doesn't change the model weights — but the runtime stores quantized activation deltas, so we advise rerun of critical eval sets after quantize.
00:55:41 Sofia: in terms of artifact delivery — how do we actually get the files into the airgapped environment?
00:56:01 Priya: we provide two options: 1) secure courier: encrypted external SSD with the archive and a manifest, signed by Redwood; 2) direct download from a customer-controlled mirror via an internal admin URL — you'd provide the mirror and credentials, and we'll push the artifact package there. both options include SHA256 manifest and PGP signature.
00:56:34 Ravi: for option 1, any tamper-evidence? chain of custody?
00:56:47 Priya: yes, chain of custody docs are included; each drive is sealed, we provide a signed manifest and a tamper-evident seal id you can verify on receipt. you'll also have a contact at Redwood to validate the seal id.
01:02:10 Emma: one more compliance detail — logs and audit trails: what does Redwood ship? is there an agent or do we pull them out?
01:02:29 Luis: we ship a lightweight agent that writes structured audit logs to a local file or syslog — we include rotation and encrypt-at-rest guidance. in air-gap mode we do not send logs back to Redwood unless you allow a push; logs include activation events, license checks, runtime restarts and perf regressions.
01:06:03 Jordan: ok great, wrapping up — action items: Priya will send the bundle + checksum and install runbook, Jordan will send license pricing and SOC2 doc, Tom will open the PO and confirm hardware inventory. we'll aim to run the bench week of 2025-10-20. thanks everyone.

ACTION-ITEMS (verbatim): Priya: send driver bundle and SHA256, Jordan: pricing & SOC2, Tom: PO and hardware list.

questions: Can we revoke an offline license if a machine is decommissioned?
What driver versions are recommended for Ampere GPUs in air-gapped mode?
How long does KV cache warmup take for typical prompt sets?
